reference.title: Map organization rules
reference.shortdesc: When organizing your book map or DITA map, you should follow these rules: Sequence r

section.p: When organizing your book map or DITA map, you should follow these rules:

ul.li:
Sequence rule: Organize <topicref> elements by the user workflow. The correct sequence is Concept → Task(s) → Reference → Troubleshooting → Glossary.
For example:<map> <title>Getting Started</title> <topicref href="c_overview.dita"/> <!-- 1. Concept --> <topicref href="t_installation.dita"/> <!-- 2. Task --> <topicref href="r_system_requirements.dita"/> <!-- 3. Reference --> <topicref href="ts_common_errors.dita"/> <!-- 4. Troubleshooting --> <topicref href="g_glossary.dita"/> <!-- 5. Glossary --> </map>

Nesting rule: Nest a <topicref> under another only when a genuine dependency exists. The genuine dependency exists only when the child topic only makes sense in context of the parent.
For example:
The topics t_configure_network.dita and t_configure_security.dita only make sense as part of configuring the whole system, so they are nested under t_configuration.dita.<map> <title>Configuration Guide</title> <topicref href="t_configuration.dita"> <topicref href="t_configure_network.dita"/> <!-- makes sense under configuration --> <topicref href="t_configure_security.dita"/> <!-- only meaningful in context of configuration --> </topicref> </map>
